angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 47,771,632 km at 188.32 pc = 3.39 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48615: distance 188.324 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.053), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 188.324 +/- 9.981 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6789 +/- 0.2214 mas (same row, RUWE 1.74), 25.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 68.667 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48615: radius 68.667 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 917.273 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.084) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 47,771,632 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3836 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48615: effective temperature 3836 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.07) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48615: effective temperature 3836 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.07) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 85951: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
